findings.origin: Native PDF extraction & ledger anchor prompt (question_ledger.py)

Baseline section 13 previously failed delta validation due to table pipe corruption. Both portfolio roll-forwards (Principal book 3,845; Other financial assets 644) are arithmetically exact.

findings.finding: DeepSeek repeatedly describes the R167m impairment loss as an 'impairment release' and questions the 'sustainability of that release'. Because PBD assets have a cumulative impairment gain (+R431m), a reduction from R598m to R431m represents an impairment LOSS (P&L charge of -R167m), not an earnings release. This inverts the economic and accounting reality.
findings.impact: P&L credit charge mischaracterized as positive income; risks faulty earnings forecasting.
findings.required_correction: Reinforce in consumer_lending guidance that for POCI assets with cumulative gain allowances, downward movements are impairment LOSSES, not allowance releases.

findings.finding: DeepSeek marked Q-08aa5c3f257440ab 'resolved' while explicitly stating in its answer that the total R4,489m PBD carrying value was not visible in this capture and that scope reconciliation was being deferred to a new question. The explicit closure condition required reconciliation to the carrying value. Valid evidence anchors alone cannot substitute for satisfying closure conditions.
findings.impact: Premature closure leaves balance-sheet scope reconciliation unverified in the persistent ledger.
findings.required_correction: Instruct models that if an essential element of a closure condition remains open or is deferred to a new question, the question status MUST remain 'partial'.

findings.origin: DeepSeek model column selection & grouped header layout (outputs/pan_dense.md)
findings.evidence: PAN physical pp. 48-49; outputs/pan_dense.md Section 2 and Section 4
findings.finding: DeepSeek double-counted 1,081 oz of third-party buy-in feedstock in FY25 Group gold production, calculating 197,608 oz vs printed 196,527 oz (+1,081 oz error). The model selected the 'Group total' underground column (93,724 oz, which already rolled in the 1,081 oz buy-in) and then added the buy-in line (1,081 oz) a second time. The disjoint sum 92,643 + 2,654 + 98,636 + 1,081 + 1,513 = 196,527 oz reconciles exactly to the single ounce.
findings.impact: False allegation of +1,081 oz production discrepancy against issuer.
findings.earliest_stage: DeepSeek column selection / PDF layout flattening
findings.required_correction: Guidance to verify whether a reported total or subtotal already incorporates secondary feedstock rows before aggregating.

findings.evidence: PAN physical pp. 48-50; outputs/pan_dense.md Section 2 and Section 4
findings.finding: DeepSeek speculated that Tennant FY25 A$ all-in cost (A$1,584,835/kg) is a 'likely printing/scale error' and that the ZAR/kg to US$/oz conversion difference is an unexplained residual. Tennant surface feedstock was in initial commissioning producing only 1,513 oz (47 kg), making initial capital costs per kg naturally extreme. Group AISC converts at asset-weighted rates, not an annual average FX rate.
findings.impact: Unsubstantiated issuer reporting error allegations distract from fundamental operational ramp-up dynamics.
findings.required_correction: Enforce strict prohibition against alleging printing/scale errors without checking production denominator scale and commissioning phase disclosures.

findings.evidence: PAN physical pp. 48-49, Group Production Summary table
findings.finding: The PAN production table exhibits genuine 1-ounce subtotal variances due to integer rounding in the source document (105,479 vs 105,478 oz; 118,852 vs 118,853 oz; 272,311 vs 272,310 oz). Furthermore, MTR FY25 tailings exhibits an internal source inconsistency: Column 6 (Surface operations) prints 25,043 oz while Column 14 (Total operations MTR total) prints 30,806 oz (difference 5,763 oz, which equals the FY26 MTR buy-in volume). The printed Surface operations total of 98,636 oz foots using the 30,806 oz figure, proving an internal source layout anomaly.
findings.impact: Clarifies issuer source table characteristics; neither DeepSeek nor Codex had forensically isolated the 5,763 oz MTR column variance.

findings.finding: Multi-tier grouped column headers (e.g. 3-tier hierarchies across 16 columns) cannot be cleanly represented in standard GitHub Flavored Markdown tables without colspan. Attempting complex programmatic table reconstruction across arbitrary company formats introduces fragile edge cases. Source layout limitations should be carried as documented analytical uncertainty, supported by targeted prompt instructions on multi-tier column selection.
findings.impact: Avoids over-engineering table parsers; preserves generic, robust extraction.
